title: Put a rook behind a pawn
objective: Place a rook behind a passed pawn so it keeps protecting the pawn as it advances.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original practice lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original practice position and teaching text; not a historical game

steps.explanation: Your a5 pawn is a passed pawn: no black pawn is in its file or either neighbouring file ahead of it. Put your rook on the a-file behind it.

question.prompt: Move the rook from b1 to a1 to support the pawn from behind.
hints: A rook protects pieces along a clear file.

tree.feedback: Ra1 protects a5 from behind along the a-file.
Rb5 protects a5 from the side. Put the rook behind the pawn so it can keep supporting further advances.

steps.explanation: Black moved the king to g8. Your rook is behind the pawn on the same file. Advance the pawn and see how the rook still protects its new square.

question.prompt: Advance your passed pawn one square.
hints: The a6 square is empty and safe.

tree.feedback: a6 advances the pawn, and the rook on a1 still protects it along the clear a-file.
Ra4 keeps the rook behind the pawn, but this task asks you to advance the pawn itself.

takeaway: A rook behind a passed pawn can keep protecting it as it advances. Check that the file is clear and the next square is safe.
